grasper_top.shaft: blue-grey / slate-grey shaft with a teal tint (pale silver-grey when close to the lens, e.g. f14-19 and f175-246; dark slate when farther, e.g. f120-170); short silver tip with short serrated jaws (ridges visible at f25, f143). Diameter guess 5 mm (could be 10 mm: it often looks 1.5-2x wider than the right instrument, but it is usually much closer to the camera).
grasper_top.notes: Enters at f13 from the top-left, passing very close to the lens: f13-17 it is an overexposed white wedge on the left (no prompts there; first prompt f19). Leaves through the top after f56 (absent f57-113). Re-enters at the top at f114-115 (rounded tip at the top edge, x~290-355), motion-blurred at f116; first prompt f118. f229-231 the shaft comes in from the top-left corner (camera roll/reposition), so f230 has its own prompt. f226 the shaft runs almost to the bottom edge (tip near (320,330)). The tip is usually pressed into the gallbladder wall, so the jaws are often hidden or covered by specular glare. Probably the same tool also shows as a small sliver at the top edge in f1-4 (x 340-390, y 0-20); not prompted. f110-113 show a blurred, serrated vertical edge near x 300-370 at the top that could be this grasper coming back or could be the gallbladder edge; not counted. Identity across the f57-113 gap is assumed (same entry direction, same shaft colour, same short serrated jaws): medium confidence on that link. The type (grasper) has medium-high confidence.

dissector_right.shaft: dark grey-green (teal-black) shaft, about 5 mm, with a bright silver distal section (collar + long, curved, tapered jaws about 4-6 shaft diameters long that open to ~90 deg). When open or close to the lens the jaws are overexposed white (f63-72, f85-92, f135-162).
dissector_right.notes: Curved Maryland/Kelly-type dissector used as the second grasping instrument for the derotation (it holds the neck/hilar side while grasper_top holds the body). The type is medium confidence: it could also be a long-jaw curved grasper. The shaft comes in from the right edge (upper third); in f165-170 and f194-212 it comes from the top-right corner. Absent f116-121. f122-127 only the dark shaft is visible in the upper right (tip behind the gallbladder); tip visible again from f128 (prompt). f132-162 the shaft is out of frame on the right and only the two long silver jaws are visible (prompts on the jaws at f145). f171-183 it is only partly in view at the top edge (jaw tips / shaft cut by the frame border), and f184-193 only the shaft is visible in the top-right (tip behind the gallbladder; prompt f186). f217-221 and f229-231 only the open jaw tips are visible as small silver slivers at the top-right edge (x 460-560, y 0-35); they have small 2-point prompts (f219, f230), which are low confidence. f232-246: a thin dark curved line in the top-right corner (x 570-600) looks like a tissue fold, not this instrument; not counted.

notes: No cuts, wipes or jump cuts found in the 247 frames. Method: every frame was looked at in 42-frame contact sheets, every 5th frame larger, plus close-ups of all jumps flagged by consecutive-frame metrics (HSV-histogram correlation, mean abs diff, ORB+RANSAC homography inliers, and a DIS optical-flow warp residual: median 5.3, max 18.4 at f193, so there is no outlier the size of a cut). The flagged frames are all continuous fast motion or appearance changes, not shot changes: f4->5 (the gallbladder is turned quickly and auto-exposure changes; background and the right instrument are continuous), f13-18 (grasper_top passes overexposed right in front of the lens; this is the lowest histogram correlation, 0.85), f55-58 (fast pan/zoom-out), f105-116 (the gallbladder rolls over while the camera follows), f170-176 (motion blur during a fast move), f192-194 (fast pan, largest flow residual), f228-231 (quick instrument move plus a small camera roll). Only two instruments appear; no third tool, gauze, clip applier or suction is seen. The black glossy blob at the bottom-left in f116-130 is fluid or the necrotic underside, not an instrument. All coordinates are integers in original 640x360 pixels. They were checked on 2x and 4x zoomed overlays, with a colour mask for teal-grey/silver metal used as a guide. Positive points sit on shaft or jaw metal, and points on large overexposed areas were moved to the darker metal next to them where possible. Negative points are on gallbladder, liver, fat or the other instrument.
